article.title: Afghanistan-Pakistan trade declines sharply as border crossings remain closed
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Dari article.
Trade between Afghanistan and Pakistan has declined sharply amid rising tensions between the neighboring countries and the continued closure of border crossings.
Mohammad Younus Mohmand, Vice President of the Afghan Chapter of the Pakistan-Afghanistan Joint Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said that the bilateral trade has fallen by about 95 percent.
“We no longer have trade with Pakistan. Our transit via Pakistan and Pakistan’s transit via Afghanistan to Central Asia have come to a complete halt,” Mohmand said.

Pakistani newspaper Dawn reported Monday that the figures released by the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan in August showed that bilateral trade between the two neighboring countries fell 95 percent in 2026-27 compared with the previous year.
The TDAP also reported that bilateral trade fell to $358 million in fiscal year 2025-26, down from $1.3 billion in fiscal year 2024-25, a decrease of about 74 percent.
Pakistan closed the main border crossings with Afghanistan on Oct. 12, 2025, after deadly clashes between the Pakistani forces and the Afghan Taliban.
In September, Pakistani government said that it was ready to reopen the border crossings if the Taliban took measures against the militant groups operating from Afghanistan.

Relations between Pakistan and the Taliban deteriorated as Pakistani authorities accused the Taliban of harboring the militant group, Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP, which has taken responsibility for attacks inside Pakistan.
The Taliban publicly deny harboring any militant group, but a U.N. report, released in August, said that the Taliban continue to support TTP.
The closure of the border crossings has hurt Pakistani industries, particularly pharmaceuticals, according to government data.

Pakistan's Dawn newspaper, citing Pakistan's Bureau of Statistics, said pharmaceutical exports declined 25.53 percent in the first quarter of 2026-27, which is primarily attributed to the disruption of trade with Afghanistan.
Mohmand said that the Taliban’s government was seeking alternative trade routes, but “Pakistani traders are at a loss.”
“I think the Pakistani traders have lost and continue to lose the 40-million-people market of Afghanistan,” he added.

Azarakhsh Hafizi, an economist and former head of the international relations committee at Afghanistan's Chamber of Commerce and Industries, told VOA that the halt in bilateral trade is “not in the interest of” either Afghanistan or Pakistan.
“Pakistani industries not only reach Afghan markets but also export via Afghanistan to Central Asia,” he added.
Hafizi said that Afghanistan’s exports via Pakistan were valued at around $1 billion and Pakistan was one of the largest destinations for Afghan products in 2024, with exports totaling $659 million.
Momand said that he “hopes the tensions between the two neighboring countries end soon.”
zh: 由於邊境口岸持續關閉，阿富汗與巴基斯坦之間的貿易量急劇下降
編者註：本文翻譯自美國之音（VOA）達里語原文報導。
隨著阿富汗與巴基斯坦兩國間的緊張局勢加劇，加上邊境口岸持續關閉，兩國之間的貿易量已大幅下滑。
巴基斯坦－阿富汗聯合工商會阿富汗分會副會長穆罕默德·尤努斯·莫曼德表示，雙邊貿易額已下降約95％。
「我們已不再與巴基斯坦進行貿易。我們經由巴基斯坦的過境貿易，以及巴基斯坦經由阿富汗前往中亞的過境貿易，都已完全中斷，」莫曼德表示。
巴基斯坦《黎明報》週一報導，根據巴基斯坦貿易發展局八月公佈的數據顯示，2026-27年度這兩國鄰國之間的雙邊貿易額較前一年度下降了95%。
TDAP 還指出，雙邊貿易額在 2025-26 財政年度降至 3.58 億美元，較 2024-25 財政年度的 13 億美元減少了約 74%。
2025年10月12日，在巴基斯坦軍隊與阿富汗塔利班爆發致命衝突後，巴基斯坦關閉了與阿富汗的主要邊境口岸。
九月，巴基斯坦政府表示，若塔利班針對從阿富汗境內活動的武裝組織採取行動，巴方便準備重新開放邊境口岸。
巴基斯坦與塔利班的關係惡化，因為巴基斯坦當局指控塔利班庇護了武裝組織「巴基斯坦塔利班運動」（Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan，簡稱TTP），該組織已宣稱對巴基斯坦境內的襲擊事件負責。
塔利班公開否認庇護任何武裝組織，但一份於八月發布的聯合國報告指出，塔利班仍持續支持巴基斯坦塔利班組織（TTP）。
根據政府數據，邊境口岸的關閉已對巴基斯坦各產業造成衝擊，尤其是製藥業。
巴基斯坦《黎明報》援引巴基斯坦統計局數據指出，2026-27年度第一季的製藥業出口額下降了25.53%，這主要歸因於與阿富汗的貿易中斷。
莫曼德表示，塔利班政府正在尋求替代貿易路線，但「巴基斯坦商人卻束手無策」。
「我認為巴基斯坦商人已經失去了阿富汗這個擁有4,000萬人口的市場，而且仍在持續失去這個市場，」他補充道。
經濟學家、阿富汗工商會前國際關係委員會主席阿扎拉克什·哈菲齊（Azarakhsh Hafizi）向美國之音表示，雙邊貿易的中斷「不符合」阿富汗或巴基斯坦任何一方的利益。
他補充道：「巴基斯坦的工業產品不僅打入阿富汗市場，還透過阿富汗出口至中亞。」
哈菲齊表示，阿富汗經由巴基斯坦出口的貨物總值約為10億美元，而巴基斯坦是2024年阿富汗產品的最大出口目的地之一，出口總額達6.59億美元。
莫曼德表示，他「希望這兩國鄰國之間的緊張局勢能早日結束」。
